final_message:
The bug was in `collect` in `billing/payments.py`. The reproduction test now passes, along with the 24 existing tests (25 in total).

When the gateway declined a charge, `collect` took an empty `else: pass` branch and never called `record_failure`. So the subscription never went to `past_due`, and the invoice never got a retry scheduled (`attempt_count` and `next_attempt_at` stayed unset). I replaced the `pass` with `record_failure(ctx, invoice, result["failure_code"])`.

I ran your test as a temporary file in `tests/` and then deleted it, so it isn't in the suite. I also wrote `answer.json` in the repo root with `{"file": "payments.py", "function": "collect"}`.

steps.command: cd billing && ls && wc -l *.py && grep -n "past_due\|def advance\|retry" *.py ../tests/conftest.py
cd billing && cat dunning.py payments.py; sed -n 55,105p engine.py
cd billing && cat dunning.py payments.py; sed -n 25,45p ../tests/conftest.py

cd .. && python - <<'E'
p='billing/payments.py'
s=open(p).read()
s=s.replace("    else:\n        pass\n","    else:\n        record_failure(ctx, invoice, result[\"failure_code\"])\n")
open(p,'w').write(s)
E
echo '{"file": "payments.py", "function": "collect"}' > answer.json
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -5

cat >> tests/test_recovery_tmp.py <<'E'
def test_recovery_after_retry_succeeds(world):
    cus = world.customer()
    world.gateway.fail_next.append("card_declined")
    sub = world.engine.subscribe(cus["id"], [(world.monthly["id"], 1)])
    assert sub["status"] == "past_due"
    world.advance_days(1)
    assert sub["status"] == "active"
    [inv] = world.engine.invoices_for(cus["id"])
    assert inv["status"] == "paid"
E
.venv/bin/python -m pytest -q 2>&1 | tail -5; rm tests/test_recovery_tmp.py
